findings.issue_text: [High/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~175 — `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, but `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (modified to run exactly when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, i.e., when the V2 evaluator is in play) calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`. With `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, this branch will throw on client deletion (failing/rolling back the delete), and in any case V2 performs no cleanup of the removed client's authz resources/policies. The override should delete the client's resource/policies (or no-op) instead of throwing.

[Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~82–92 — `canMapRoles`/`canMapCompositeRoles`/`canMapClientScopeRoles` check only fine-grained grants and, unlike every other method in this class (`canManage`, `canManageClientScopes`, `canView(ClientScope)`, …), omit the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role bypass. Under V2's default-deny semantics this denies all client role-mapping operations to users holding the `manage-clients` role — including cross-realm/master admins, for whom `hasPermission()` unconditionally returns `false` via the `isAdminSameRealm()` check — unless an explicit permission exists. Likely a functional regression vs. V1 (where clients without permissions enabled are unrestricted).

[Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~139–185 — Runtime evaluation/query methods (`canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `managePermission`, `viewPermission`, `configurePermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `exchangeToPermission`, `resource`) throw `UnsupportedOperationException` instead of failing closed. These are invoked from live code paths (e.g., the token-exchange flow calling `canExchangeTo`, admin console/API calling `isPermissionsEnabled`/`getPermissions`), which will produce 500 errors rather than a 403/deny when the feature is enabled. They should return `false`/deny or be implemented.

[Low/performance] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~110–137 — `getClientsWithPermission` performs a full policy evaluation (`root.evaluatePermission`) per resource via `hasGrantedPermission`; used for filtering client lists this is O(n) evaluations per request, and single checks like `canView(client)` can trigger 2–3 separate evaluations (`canView()` type-level, `canManage(client)`, per-client `VIEW`). Consider a single batched evaluation or short-circuit ordering.

[Low/data] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~118–126 — `resourceStore.findByType(server, CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` also matches the type-level "all clients" resource itself (name `"Clients"`). When a type-level policy grants the scope, the literal string `"Clients"` is added to the returned set of client IDs (a nonexistent client), while the actual clients covered by that type-level grant are not returned — consumers receive a bogus ID and misleading results.

[Low/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~255 — dead code: private `getEvaluationContext(...)` is never called (it only matters for the unimplemented `canExchangeTo`); the `logger` field and the static import of `AdminPermissionManagement.TOKEN_EXCHANGE` are also unused.

[Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java — the new `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope (`canMapClientScopeRoles`) has no test coverage anywhere in the diff; only `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` are exercised.

[Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java (testManageAllClients) — no test deletes a client that actually has client-level permissions/resources granted (the deleted `newClient` has none), so cleanup on client removal (the behavior that `setPermissionsEnabled` is supposed to provide) is never verified.

goldens.comment: Inconsistent feature flag bug causing orphaned permissions. The AdminPermissions event listener, responsible for cleaning up permissions upon role, client, or group removal, is incorrectly guarded by the ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ (V1) feature flag. This is inconsistent with other methods in the class that use ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2. Consequently, if ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2 is enabled but V1 is not, the permission cleanup logic will not execute, leading to orphaned permission data. Cleanup should occur regardless of which fine-grained authorization version is enabled.

In hasPermission(ClientModel client, String scope), the resource lookup uses findByName(server, client.getId(), server.getId()), but AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource creates per-client resources with the owner set to resourceServer.getClientId(), so this lookup will never find those resources and will always fall back to the 'all-clients' resource, effectively ignoring client-specific permissions.

In getClientsWithPermission(String scope), iterating resourceStore.findByType(server, AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE) and returning resource.getName() will only ever consider the type-level 'Clients' resource (per-client resources have no type) and return its name, while AvailableRoleMappingResource#getRoleIdsWithPermissions expects actual client IDs to pass to realm.getClientById, which can lead to incorrect behavior or a null client and subsequent failures.

In ClientPermissionsV2.hasPermission, the method getResourceTypeResource could return null, leading to a NullPointerException in findByResource. Defensive null checks are needed to prevent this issue.
Remove unused getEvaluationContext private method in ClientPermissionsV2 - it is defined but never called

adjudication_records.issue_text: [High/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~175 — `setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`, but `AdminPermissions.registerListener` (modified to run exactly when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, i.e., when the V2 evaluator is in play) calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(client, false)` on `ClientRemovedEvent`. With `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` now returning `ClientPermissionsV2`, this branch will throw on client deletion (failing/rolling back the delete), and in any case V2 performs no cleanup of the removed client's authz resources/policies. The override should delete the client's resource/policies (or no-op) instead of throwing.

adjudication.rationale: In the diff, `AdminPermissions.registerListener` is changed to execute its event handling only when `Profile.Feature.ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` is enabled, and in the `ClientRemovedEvent` branch it calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`. Also in the diff, `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` is overridden to return `ClientPermissionsV2`, and `ClientPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled(ClientModel, boolean)` unconditionally throws `UnsupportedOperationException`. Therefore, in the V2/feature-enabled path where `MgmtPermissionsV2` is used, a client removal event will trigger a call path that throws, potentially breaking client deletion/cleanup. This is a concrete behavioral failure grounded in the shown changes.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~82–92 — `canMapRoles`/`canMapCompositeRoles`/`canMapClientScopeRoles` check only fine-grained grants and, unlike every other method in this class (`canManage`, `canManageClientScopes`, `canView(ClientScope)`, …), omit the `MANAGE_CLIENTS` admin-role bypass. Under V2's default-deny semantics this denies all client role-mapping operations to users holding the `manage-clients` role — including cross-realm/master admins, for whom `hasPermission()` unconditionally returns `false` via the `isAdminSameRealm()` check — unless an explicit permission exists. Likely a functional regression vs. V1 (where clients without permissions enabled are unrestricted).

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2`, the role-mapping checks (`canMapRoles`, `canMapCompositeRoles`, `canMapClientScopeRoles`) simply `return hasPermission(client, ...)` and do not include the admin-role bypass that other methods in the same class implement (e.g., `canManage(ClientModel)` checks `root.hasOneAdminRole(AdminRoles.MANAGE_CLIENTS)` first; `canManageClientScopes()` and `canView(ClientScopeModel)` also special-case admin roles). Since `hasPermission(ClientModel, ...)` immediately returns `false` when `!root.isAdminSameRealm()`, an admin with `MANAGE_CLIENTS` (including cross-realm/master admin scenarios) would be denied these role-mapping operations under V2 unless an explicit fine-grained permission exists. This inconsistency is directly verifiable from the added code and would cause incorrect authorization decisions.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Medium/bug] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~139–185 — Runtime evaluation/query methods (`canExchangeTo`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `getPermissions`, `managePermission`, `viewPermission`, `configurePermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `exchangeToPermission`, `resource`) throw `UnsupportedOperationException` instead of failing closed. These are invoked from live code paths (e.g., the token-exchange flow calling `canExchangeTo`, admin console/API calling `isPermissionsEnabled`/`getPermissions`), which will produce 500 errors rather than a 403/deny when the feature is enabled. They should return `false`/deny or be implemented.

adjudication.rationale: The diff clearly shows `ClientPermissionsV2` is newly introduced and wired into `MgmtPermissionsV2.clients()` (so it can be used at runtime), while a number of overridden methods (`canExchangeTo`, `exchangeToPermission`, `mapRolesPermission`, `managePermission`, `configurePermission`, `viewPermission`, `isPermissionsEnabled`, `setPermissionsEnabled`, `resource`, `getPermissions`, etc.) unconditionally throw `UnsupportedOperationException`. That is a concrete incompleteness/risk: if any existing admin/token-exchange code path calls these methods when V2 is active, it will yield 500s. However, the finding’s specific claim that these are invoked from “live code paths (e.g., token-exchange flow, admin console/API calling isPermissionsEnabled/getPermissions)” is not verifiable from the provided diff alone (no call sites shown), so it can’t be confirmed as a definite introduced defect purely from this diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/performance] services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/ClientPermissionsV2.java:~110–137 — `getClientsWithPermission` performs a full policy evaluation (`root.evaluatePermission`) per resource via `hasGrantedPermission`; used for filtering client lists this is O(n) evaluations per request, and single checks like `canView(client)` can trigger 2–3 separate evaluations (`canView()` type-level, `canManage(client)`, per-client `VIEW`). Consider a single batched evaluation or short-circuit ordering.

adjudication.rationale: In `ClientPermissionsV2#getClientsWithPermission`, the method iterates all resources of type `AdminPermissionsSchema.CLIENTS_RESOURCE_TYPE` via `resourceStore.findByType(...)` and for each calls `hasGrantedPermission(...)`, which performs `root.evaluatePermission(new ResourcePermission(...))`. This is clearly one full permission evaluation per client resource (O(n) evaluations per call). Also, per-client checks can stack multiple evaluations: `canView(client)` may call `canView()` (which can call `hasPermission(AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW)` -> evaluation) and/or `canConfigure(client)` -> `canManage(client)` -> `hasPermission(client, MANAGE)` plus `hasPermission(client, CONFIGURE)`, each of which evaluates permissions separately. This is a diff-grounded performance/architecture concern rather than a correctness defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java — the new `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` scope (`canMapClientScopeRoles`) has no test coverage anywhere in the diff; only `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` are exercised.

adjudication.rationale: The diff introduces a new scope constant `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in `AdminPermissionsSchema` and adds logic for it in `ClientPermissionsV2#canMapClientScopeRoles(ClientModel)` (checks `hasPermission(client, AdminPermissionsSchema.MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE)`). However, the added/modified tests only exercise `MAP_ROLES` and `MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE` (e.g., `PermissionClientTest#testMapRolesAndCompositesOnlyOneClient` grants `Set.of(MAP_ROLES, MAP_ROLES_COMPOSITE, CONFIGURE)`), and there is no usage of `MAP_ROLES_CLIENT_SCOPE` in the test changes shown. This is a concrete missing-test gap for newly added authorization behavior, not a functional defect by itself.

adjudication_records.issue_text: [Low/test_gap] tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/PermissionClientTest.java (testManageAllClients) — no test deletes a client that actually has client-level permissions/resources granted (the deleted `newClient` has none), so cleanup on client removal (the behavior that `setPermissionsEnabled` is supposed to provide) is never verified.

adjudication.rationale: In `PermissionClientTest#testManageAllClients`, the test grants an *all-clients* permission via `createAllPermission(client, clientsType, ..., Set.of(MANAGE))`, then creates and deletes `newClient`. It never creates a client-specific permission/resource tied to `newClient` (e.g., `createPermission(client, newClientId, clientsType, ...)`), so deleting `newClient` does not exercise/verify any cleanup of client-level authz artifacts that would be triggered on `ClientRemovedEvent` (the listener calls `management(...).clients().setPermissionsEnabled(cast.getClient(), false)`). The new tests added also don’t delete a client after granting client-specific permissions (e.g., `testManageOnlyOneClient` grants permission to `myclient` but does not remove it).
